name: Clothing Edge Blend
description: Scrutinizes transition zones between clothing boundaries and background regions for alpha-blending artifacts and inconsistent edge feathering common in body-swap deepfake synthesis.
algorithm: Clothing Edge Blend — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes clothing-body edge blending for deepfake detection following Rossler et al. (2019):

1. **Clothing Boundary Detection**: The boundary between clothing and body/face regions is detected per frame using semantic segmentation. Clothing edges (collar-neck junction, sleeve-arm boundary, neckline) are extracted and parameterized.

2. **Edge Blend Zone Analysis**: In authentic video, clothing-body boundaries show physically correct transitions — fabric partially occluding skin, compression of fabric at pressure points, natural draping creating soft shadows. The method measures the blend zone width, gradient profile, and shadow consistency at clothing boundaries.

3. **Face-Swap Boundary Detection**: Face-swap deepfakes must blend the generated face with the original body/clothing. The method specifically examines the collar-neck-jawline junction where this blending occurs. Artifacts include: unnatural alpha blending gradients, color temperature discontinuities, and resolution mismatches between generated face and original clothing.

4. **Temporal Edge Coherence**: Clothing-body edges should move coherently with body motion. The method tracks edge positions across frames and measures temporal consistency. Deepfake artifacts may cause clothing edges to flicker, teleport, or exhibit motion decoupled from the body's physical movement.

5. **Occlusion Consistency**: Natural clothing creates consistent occlusion patterns — a collar always covers the same neck region from a given angle. The method checks whether occlusion relationships between clothing and body remain physically consistent across frames and head pose changes. Deepfakes may produce impossible occlusion states where generated face regions incorrectly overlap with original clothing.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through clothing edge blend analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
